name: maybe_Fs_SetTransferPriority
summary: Enables or disables the twelve transfer channels from the 5-bytes-per-mode table at 0x72D710 and, when the mode reaches 4, arms the bulk transfer (0x10E5D8) with the pair at +0x10/+0x14 or cancels it (0x10E64C).
evidence: The only in-engine caller is now named Fs_CacheSet_Initialize (0x103724), so a cache-set transfer setup is plausible, but nothing in the body names a priority or the channels; wording kept as a hypothesis.

name: Fs_Initialize
summary: Brings up the filesystem subsystem: waits for runtime init, opens the "fs:USER" service session, stores the archive/file handles, initialises the intrusive list and flushes one system-info query.
evidence: The string passed to 0x0011CCA0 is the literal "fs:USER" (read from code.bin at 0x0072FC13, not visible in the decompiler output), which makes this nn::fs initialisation rather than a generic file open; the old name's 'OpenSubsystemFiles' is close but the session string pins it down.

name: maybe_Os_ShutdownSyncObject
summary: Tears the global sync object down: closes every registered handle through 0x0011C814, unlinks the node at 0x7E79D8, issues svcCloseHandle (svc 0x23) for the pending handle and clears the global state word under the exclusive-access lock.
evidence: No caller (it is an atexit/hook slot); the body only closes handles and clears state, so the first pass's 'signal' wording was wrong (renamed to Shutdown), but the object's identity is still unknown.

name: maybe_Gfx_SetFrameReadyFlag
signature: void maybe_Gfx_SetFrameReadyFlag(GfxDisplay* self, FrameRecord* rec, u8 value)
summary: Stores the value in the frame record's +0x11 byte and, while the display state is 0x300, takes the GPU lock (0x1197FC), executes the command list and releases it (0x11980C).
evidence: Still no caller; the named callee Gfx_ExecuteCommandList places it in the frame submission path, but the 'ready' meaning of +0x11 remains inferred.

name: maybe_Gfx_ConvertTextureBlock
signature: int maybe_Gfx_ConvertTextureBlock(int width, int height, int decodeNow, unsigned int size)
summary: Builds a decoder object whose type tag is the 4CC "HTP" (0x00780EAC), feeds it a 0x28-byte block header, optionally converts one block and returns width*0x20 + height*0x18 + blockIndex, i.e. a tile-format byte size.
evidence: The type tag at 0x00780EAC spells "HTP" and the callee is Gfx_IpcCmd803, so the old 'Snd stream decoder' name had the wrong subsystem; the exact codec (texture block vs. tile strip) is still open, hence only 0.35.

name: maybe_Gfx_SubmitValueCommand
summary: Stores the value at +0x10 of the record and submits {value} with command header 0x0B0501C8 through 0x00111B40 (Gfx_IpcCmd861).
evidence: Neither the body nor the callee carries a name or channel index, so the old 'RegisterChannelName' claim was unsupported; only the store plus GPU command submission is verified and there are no callers.

name: maybe_Gfx_InitFrameBuffers
summary: One-shot setup: takes six values from the display IPC query (0x001125C8), copies the 0x2b0-byte command block into the set and derives the five sub-buffer pointers at 0, 0xa8, 0x108, 0x158 and 0x238.
evidence: The only support for the framebuffer reading is the paired teardown 0x10C0D8 (called from maybe_Gfx_ReleaseRenderer); the body itself only moves query results into the set, so the name stays a hypothesis.

name: Gfx_FreeFrameBuffers
summary: Closes the five display handles stored at indices 0,2,4,7,9, destroys the mutex at +0x2b, closes the last IPC handle and clears the one-shot init flag at 0x7AEA70.
evidence: Exact mirror image of 0x10BFB0's layout (same five indices plus the mutex) and its caller is now named maybe_Gfx_ReleaseRenderer, so the alloc/free pair is established even though the individual handles are unnamed.

name: maybe_Svc_SyncObject_DestroyA
summary: Destructor of a small handle-owning object: tears the kernel object down with Os_CloseHandleAndUnlink (0x111E44) and closes the handle at +0x14, returning the object.
evidence: No callers; the sibling 0x509B40 repeats the shape with the other sync primitive, so 'sync object' remains the previous pass's hypothesis rather than something the body proves.

name: maybe_Svc_SyncObject_DestroyC
summary: Closes the six kernel handles held at +0, +8, +0x10, +0x1C, +0x24 and +0x40 and destroys the mutex at +0x2C.
evidence: No callers and no strings; the same 'close all handles then destroy the mutex' shape as 0x509A20 supports the destructor reading, but nothing identifies the owning subsystem.

name: Input_SetPadMode
summary: Stores the raw pad mode in +0x38 and the normalised mode (0,1,2; anything else 0) in +0x70.
evidence: The named caller Input_UpdatePadState (0x108A00) calls it as the first step of the pad update and the body only normalises the 0/1/2 mode, so the previous guess is safe.

name: maybe_Gfx_NegotiateDisplayMode
signature: int maybe_Gfx_NegotiateDisplayMode(u32* outA, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, int* outB, u32* outC, u32 arg6, u32 arg7, u32 arg8)
summary: Display-transfer state machine: maps the low-level status codes 1..0x41 to engine display modes, retries transient codes and drives the enable/disable transitions around Gfx_TransferGpuBuffer.
evidence: Callers now include maybe_Gfx_HandleVBlank and the named callee Gfx_TransferGpuBuffer, which fixes the display/GPU-buffer context; 'negotiation' is still the previous pass's interpretation of the status mapping.

name: maybe_Os_OpenServiceHandle
signature: void maybe_Os_OpenServiceHandle(u32 namePtr, int arg2, int arg3)
summary: Creates three kernel objects, stores them in the globals at 0x7EDFA4, replaces two handles with the caller's values and starts the worker thread 0x00113F2C with the argument block.
evidence: The caller is now named Mem_MapSharedBlock and the body starts a thread rather than opening a named service, so 'service handle' is doubtful; no string or service name appears, hence kept as maybe.

name: Ui_DestroyRootSingleton
summary: Shutdown hook: fetches the lazily created UI root singleton and, when it exists, calls the destructor stored just before it ((vtable+4), with the pair at -8/-4).
evidence: The callee is now confidently named Ui_CreateRootSingleton and the whole body is the matching virtual-destructor dispatch, so the singleton teardown reading is supported.

name: Gfx_ReleaseGpuInterrupt
summary: Issues GPU service command 0x30000 and, on success, clears the cached interrupt counters at 0x7B2D08+4/+8; the 0x19/0xF9610C02 'already clear' results are tolerated.
evidence: Caller is now named Gfx_ShutdownChannel and the callee Gfx_IpcCmd30000 is the same 0x30000 handshake as its partner 0x111BAC (0x40000), so the interrupt-release reading holds.

name: Snd_SetOutputMode
summary: Stores the speaker configuration byte at +2 of the sound state and forwards the mode to the mixing layer under the global sound lock; returns 0 when the lock cannot be taken.
evidence: Called from the now-named Snd_InitSystemState (0x10C738) with the 3DS output mode byte and the callee is the already named maybe_Snd_SetChannelPan on the global sound system, so the old guess is supported.

name: Gfx_IpcCmd50100
summary: Thin wrapper that submits one 32-bit value as command 0x00050100 through Gfx_IpcCmd4B00C2Call(7, ...).
evidence: The sibling name Gfx_IpcCmd4B00C2Call identifies the command-table family, so the old 'Svc_' prefix implied a kernel SVC that is not used here; only caller is the display-transfer state machine 0x10CF50.

name: Gfx_FreeCommandList
summary: Releases a command-list buffer: compares the list's slot address against the bound slot, calls the release callback with the target address/size and clears the three bookkeeping words.
evidence: The caller is now named Gfx_InitCommandLists and the 0x10000/0x20000 offsets it compares against are the two framebuffer slots that routine sets up, so the teardown reading is supported.

name: maybe_Os_DestroyThreadLocal
summary: At thread exit, fetches the thread-local object (0x11F20C) and destroys it with 0x11F730 followed by 0x11F698.
evidence: No callers (it is reached from a destructor/exit hook); the two callees are still unnamed, so 'thread local' is only supported by the TLS accessor shape, not by a named neighbour.

name: maybe_Os_WaitSharedBlock
summary: Waits on the handle stored in *state with svcWaitSynchronization1 (svc 0x24), asserts on a negative result, then re-opens the SDK session with Os_EnsureIpcSessionOpen.
evidence: No callers; the two parts (svc 0x24 wait plus the named Os_EnsureIpcSessionOpen) confirm the sync/session shape, but what is being waited on is still unknown.

name: maybe_Os_SignalEvent
summary: Signals the pending GPU event under the scheduler lock: calls 0x11A3B0 (Gfx_IpcCmd430040), closes the stale handle, and waits on the completion handle at 0x7AF0C8 (svc 0x14).
evidence: The decompilation is damaged (in_r3/unaff_r4/in_lr flag registers), so despite the named caller 0x10CF50 the body cannot be read reliably; confidence kept low.

name: Mem_MapPages
signature: int Mem_MapPages(MemPageBlock* block, unsigned int size, unsigned char flags)
summary: Allocates a page-aligned range for the block (Mem_AllocAddressRange) and maps it with svcMapMemoryBlock (svc 0x1F), recording the flags and marking +0x18 mapped.
evidence: The 0xFFF alignment check, the named Mem_AllocAddressRange and the svc 0x1F mapping step are all visible in the body, which is exactly the page-mapping idiom; no caller yet.

name: Snd_UpdateChannelState
summary: Commits one sound channel's pending updates: each dirty bit (matrix, gain, mode, loop points, ADPCM parameters, wave data) calls the matching Snd_SetChannel* writer, then recomputes the mix command size and clears the dirty mask.
evidence: The dirty-bit dispatch now calls the confidently named maybe_Snd_SetChannelMatrix / Param1 / Param2 / LoopPoints / AdpcmParams / Mode / WaveData helpers, and the caller Sound_Channel_ReleaseAll is named.

name: Os_QueryTime
signature: void Os_QueryTime(OsTime* out, u32 arg2, int mode)
summary: Queries the current system time into eight words, then normalises the packed date flags: empty fields become -1 and the flag bits are split out of the values.
evidence: The taker is the named Os_IpcQueryCommand18 and the caller is maybe_Gfx_GetEventData; the 0x70/7 bit fields are the SDK packed-time flags, so 'query time' is well supported though the struct meaning stays partial.

name: Snd_ListInsertByPriority
summary: Inserts an entry into the priority-ordered sound list at the first position whose clamped priority is lower (or equal in strict mode) than the new entry's, then links it with 0x11FCF8.
evidence: The caller is now the confidently named Sound_Voice_InsertByPriority (0.85), which does the same insertion for voices, so this is the list-level helper it uses.

name: Gfx_SetFrameColorParam
signature: void Gfx_SetFrameColorParam(void* self, const u8* arg2)
summary: Sets the frame's colour parameter: calls the device vtable +0x14 with (self->f_10, 2) and copies the two colour bytes into the current frame record at +0x126/+0x12A.
evidence: Four callers are now named, including maybe_Ui_ScreenEffect_ApplyFrameColor and Ui_MessageWindow_UpdateInput, and the caller builds the {3,0xFF,0xFF,...} fade record - which supports the colour reading.

name: Fs_ResourceFindInBucket
signature: int Fs_ResourceFindInBucket(ResourceTable* self, int bucket, u32 name)
summary: Scans one hash bucket of the resource table and returns the first entry that Fs_ResourceFindByName matches, or null.
evidence: The callee is now the confidently named Fs_ResourceFindByName (0.65) and the body is exactly that lookup over one bucket; no direct caller, but the helper's role is no longer in doubt.

name: Video_ConvertStripTo16bpp
summary: Converts one source strip into the destination frame: runs 0x100 fixed-point (Q15) rotation/mix steps and writes a clamped 16-bit sample per step.
evidence: Its caller is now named Gfx_Movie_ConvertSliceRowsTo16bpp (0.5), which prepares 0x1D0-byte per-column work items with a 2-byte destination step, so the 16 bpp strip conversion is supported.

name: Script_CallAllArgs
summary: Calls the closure currently on top of the VM stack with every pushed argument (top-1 parameters) and returns 1 on success or -1 on failure.
evidence: The callee is now the confidently named Script_Vm_CallClosure (0.8) and the body is the standard 'resolve stack top, call with that many parameters' adaptor.

name: Script_CallAllArgsNoThrow
summary: Same as Script_CallAllArgs but passes raiseError = 0 to Script_Vm_CallClosure, so a failing closure returns -1 instead of raising.
evidence: The fourth argument of the now-named Script_Vm_CallClosure is raiseError and this wrapper passes 0, which matches the old 'NoThrow' reading exactly.

name: maybe_Script_NewSlot
summary: Bound Squirrel helper: calls Script_Vm_NewSlot and turns its negative result into -1 (raise) or 1 (success).
evidence: The callee is now confidently named Script_Vm_NewSlot (0.85), so the operation this native exposes is new-slot, not a generic 'API result check'; the argument registers are lost so the wrapper's exact stack contract is unverified.

name: Sound_DecodeBufferInit
signature: u32 Sound_DecodeBufferInit(SoundVoice* self, u32 blockSize, u32 sampleCount, u32 channels, int flag, int mode)
summary: Allocates the per-channel decode buffers of a sound voice (blockSize*(samples*1.5+1) bytes each), fills them with 0x80 silence and a 0x80 tail, and links the three shared 0x2100-byte buffers.
evidence: The caller is now named Gfx_Movie_AllocStreamObjectC, which allocates the voice and its channel pointer array first, so this is the buffer half of the stream decoder setup.

name: maybe_Script_GetInstanceUserPointer
summary: Bound Squirrel helper: calls Script_Vm_GetInstanceUserPointer and returns 1 on success or -1 on failure.
evidence: The callee is now confidently named Script_Vm_GetInstanceUserPointer (0.75), which identifies the operation; the wrapper is argument-less in the decompilation so only the return mapping is certain.

name: maybe_Script_TableRemoveKey
summary: Bound Squirrel helper: calls Script_Table_RemoveKey and returns 1 on success or -1 on failure.
evidence: The callee is now confidently named Script_Table_RemoveKey (0.72), so the old 'ApiResultOk2' wording hid which operation it wraps.

name: maybe_UndecodedCallback
summary: Bytes at 0x00152EA8 do not decode as a function in the Ghidra project (halt_baddata); it is reached as a callback target from 0x006B95E4, so it is probably code reached through a thunk or a literal pool.
evidence: The body is still only halt_baddata() and the bytes were not disassembled by hand, so no behavioural name is possible; the old 'Game_' prefix was invented and is dropped.

name: MoLive_ParseL2Header
signature: u32 MoLive_ParseL2Header(const char* data, u32* outKey, s16* outLength)
summary: Validates and decodes the 12-byte 'L2' record header: reassembles the mixed-endian key words, re-derives the 0xAAAA XOR checksum, and on a match writes the key pair and the byte-swapped length+1.
evidence: The only caller is now named MoLive_Reader_Process (0.6), the MoLive streaming reader, so the 'Pack_' prefix of the old name pointed at the wrong container format; the parser itself is unchanged.

name: Str_FreeStringList
summary: Frees a two-level string list: the first string, every string in the pointer array, then the array itself.
evidence: The caller is now named Gfx_Movie_FreeStreamObjectC, which frees the movie/stream object containing this list; the body is a textbook three-level free.

name: maybe_Script_ReturnZeroStub
summary: Bound native that performs the slot store Script_SetSlotFromStack and then returns 0 unconditionally.
evidence: The callee is now named Script_SetSlotFromStack, but the native's purpose (why it always returns 0) is still unknown and it has no caller in the readable tree, so the name keeps its maybe_ prefix.

name: maybe_Script_GetInstance
summary: Bound Squirrel helper: calls Script_Vm_GetInstance and maps a negative result to -1, success to 1.
evidence: The callee is now confidently named Script_Vm_GetInstance (0.75), so the operation is instance extraction rather than a generic result check.

name: maybe_Script_TableGetSlot
summary: Bound Squirrel helper: calls Script_Table_GetSlot and returns 1 on success or -1 on failure.
evidence: The callee is now confidently named Script_Table_GetSlot (0.6), which fixes the operation the old 'ApiResultOk3' name left vague.

name: maybe_Script_Clone
summary: Bound Squirrel helper: calls Script_Vm_Clone and returns 1 on success or -1 on failure.
evidence: The callee is now confidently named Script_Vm_Clone (0.85) and it sits directly after Script_ToBool, so this is the clone native rather than an unnamed result check.

name: maybe_Script_PushRootTable
summary: Bound Squirrel helper: pushes the VM root table with Script_Vm_PushRootTable and always returns 1.
evidence: The callee is now confidently named Script_Vm_PushRootTable (0.85) and the 88-byte body is only that call plus 'return 1', so the old 'ApiCallNoArgs' wording was too vague.

name: maybe_Data_BuildTaggedRecord44
signature: void maybe_Data_BuildTaggedRecord44(u32* out, u32 first, u32 second)
summary: Builds a 0x44-byte stack record with a type-descriptor word at +0 (0x00782780) around the output of 0x006F0C10, copying 17 words out.
evidence: The body contains no matrix arithmetic, only a type tag plus a call and a word copy, and its callers are the battle model-resource binding routines - so the old 'Transform44' name claimed maths that is not there; the payload type is still unknown.

name: maybe_Script_ToStringNative
summary: Bound Squirrel helper: calls Script_Vm_ToString on the argument and returns 1.
evidence: The callee is now confidently named Script_Vm_ToString (0.85, matching sq_tostring), which directly contradicts the old 'SetStackTop' name; the argument registers are lost so only the operation is certain.

name: maybe_Script_CheckOneParam
summary: Bound Squirrel helper: calls Script_Vm_CheckParams1 and returns 1 on success or -1 when the parameter check fails.
evidence: The callee is now confidently named Script_Vm_CheckParams1 (0.75), which identifies the check; 'ApiResultCheckE' told the reader nothing.

name: Ui_GoldWindow_SetOwner
signature: void Ui_GoldWindow_SetOwner(UiGoldWindow* self, uint32_t owner, uint8_t visible)
summary: Assigns a new owning object to the gold window: when the passed handle is still live it notifies the previous owner through vtable +0x7C, then stores the visibility byte at +0x4BE.
evidence: The caller is now named Ui_CreateWindowById and calls this as the final setup step, and the live-handle check uses the same 0x7B80C0 generation table as the other engine handle users.

name: maybe_Game_QueryDataManager
summary: Calls Game_GetDataManager and passes the resulting context to func_0063CDA0, discarding the result.
evidence: The body resolves the game data manager (not battle work), and the only caller 0x001763FC is now named Field_CheckZonePoint, so 'Battle_GetWorkRef' had both the subsystem and the object wrong; the purpose of the 0x63CDA0 query is unknown.

name: maybe_Field_InitNpcAction
summary: Stores the speed value at +0x2C, plays the action animation pair (packed literals 0x74736F4C and 0x0074754E) on the NPC object at +0x28 and sets its grid state to 2.
evidence: Both callees are now named (Field_NpcPlayActionAnim, Map_PlaceObject), which supports 'NPC action setup'; note the incoming speed register is lost (in_s0), so the constructor vs. setter distinction is unverified.

name: maybe_Map_AddInstanceIfVisible
summary: Adds an instance only when the table is active (f_e0 == 1) or the kind is below 5: takes a free slot at table+0xC, assigns the generation-wrapped handle from f_e4 and calls 0x17C9F8.
evidence: The caller 0x005F4D40 is still unnamed, and f_e0 may mean visible or active, so the old 'IfVisible' wording is kept; the free-slot plus wrapping-handle logic is confirmed by the body.

name: Ui_VisitWidgets
signature: void Ui_VisitWidgets(Widget* root, int arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Walks the intrusive child list at root+0x120 and calls the layout callback 0x0053CD1C for each visible child whose vtable type is not the cached one, threading the accumulator through arg2+4.
evidence: The neighbours of this function are now named Ui_Window_* layout routines and the body is the same child-list traversal used by 0x364970, so the visitor reading is supported.

name: Ui_Window_LayoutChildren
signature: void Ui_Window_LayoutChildren(UiWindow* self, u32 rows, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Lays out a compound window: runs the base row layout, forwards the row arguments to five sub-widgets and then applies the callback to both child lists at +0x2240/+0x2298.
evidence: Every callee is now named (Ui_Window_LayoutRows plus the five measure helpers built in this batch), which pins this down as the aggregate layout override. This is not a damaged body: the unaff_r4-r8 values are the variadic arguments the function forwards to 0x0053CD1C, not lost inputs.

name: Ui_Window_MeasureContent
signature: void Ui_Window_MeasureContent(UiWindow* window, UiLayoutPass* pass, UiLayoutCtx* ctx, int flags)
summary: Measure override of the message window: when the window has content, lets the layout context accumulate the window extent and then tail-calls Ui_Window_LayoutRows.
evidence: Vtable slot +6 of 0x00768A08 is the same measure slot installed by the window constructor and filled by the 0x364970 family, and the callee is now named Ui_Window_LayoutRows.

name: Ui_Window_BindRowLayoutSources
signature: void Ui_Window_BindRowLayoutSources(UiWindow* self, u32* rowData, UiLayoutContext* ctx, UiRow* row)
summary: Resolves up to three row source pointers through the layout-context row allocator, stores the row's source block, then forwards to Ui_Window_LayoutRows.
evidence: The callee is now named Ui_Window_LayoutRows and the function is one of the measure callbacks in the same vtable group, so the binding-then-layout reading holds.

name: Ui_PartySelectWindow_BindSelectedRow
signature: void Ui_PartySelectWindow_BindSelectedRow(UiPartySelectWindow* self, u32* rowData, UiLayoutContext* ctx, u32 arg4)
summary: Binds the object of the currently selected party row (selection index at +0x194, 0xFF = none) into the layout row before laying it out.
evidence: The neighbour Ui_PartySelectWindow_Init and the 0x14-byte row table at +0x128 match the party-select window, and the callee is now named Ui_Window_LayoutRows.

name: Field_CreateActorData
signature: void* Field_CreateActorData(u32 id, const void* desc)
summary: Constructs a field actor data block through 0x00336A38 for the given id/descriptor and fills the defaults (vtable at +0, -1.0f, flags, colours); returns the interior pointer at -0x2B0.
evidence: Its caller is now named Field_Scene_AddActorObject, which allocates exactly this data block when placing an actor, so 'create actor data' is supported by the call site.

name: Text_GetLayoutStats
summary: Lazily builds the text-layout object (vtable 0x7829CC), then walks every entry and writes four counters: entry count, entry count from the layout page, empty-span count and total non-empty spans.
evidence: Disassembly shows the two per-entry calls to 0x18D5A0 only return 0/1 (a content test) and the results are summed and counted, so this is a statistics pass, not a 'measure cache'.

name: Text_SpanHasContent
signature: bool Text_SpanHasContent(const TextEntry* entry, const u32* span)
summary: Returns true when the entry's style id is below 7, its first 16-bit field is non-zero and the two words of the second span are not both zero.
evidence: Disassembly of the full 56-byte body (0x18D5A0-0x18D5D8: ldrh [r4]; ldrd [r5]; orrsne; movne r0,#1) proves a predicate returning 0/1, so the first pass's 'non-returning throw' was a misread of a truncated tail call.

name: Party_GetMemberRecord
summary: Bounds-checked accessor for the 8-slot party-member table at self+0x944C (stride 0x60); returns null when the index is negative or past the count.
evidence: The count routine 0x62A110 is called by Ui_MemberTable_Init and Ui_PartyList_InsertMember, and the table range 0x944C..0x974C is exactly 8 * 0x60, which supports the member-slot reading; the Ghidra bounds expression itself is partly mangled.

name: maybe_Party_GetMemberCount
summary: Returns the number of used party-member slots by scanning the ids at self+0x944C for the 0xff terminator, falling back to 8 when the table is empty.
evidence: Callers now include Ui_MemberTable_Init and Ui_PartyList_InsertMember, which supports 'party member count', but the decompiled loop tail is mangled into a noreturn call, so the exact counting rule is unverified.

name: maybe_Text_BuildLayoutSpanA
signature: void maybe_Text_BuildLayoutSpanA(void* self, const TextEntry* entry)
summary: Builds a text-layout span from the record passed in; the 552-byte ARM body starts with push {r4-r8,lr} and fills a stack record, but Ghidra truncated it after the first call.
evidence: The readable body is a single func_00100B74 call although the function is 552 bytes (disassembly at 0x18CEA4 starts with a six-register push), so it is a damaged decompilation; the name is a hypothesis based on the two neighbouring layout-span builders.

name: Text_InitStringRef
signature: void Text_InitStringRef(TextRef* out, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 textId)
summary: Fills a three-word text reference: two caller-supplied words plus the resolved handle from func_0051BB08(textId, 0xE, -1).
evidence: The caller is now named Text_LayoutLine_AutoSize, which uses the reference to lay out a line, so the 'init string ref' reading is supported.

name: maybe_Text_BuildLayoutSpanB
signature: void maybe_Text_BuildLayoutSpanB(void* self, const TextEntry* entry, u32 word0, u32 word1)
summary: Builds a second layout span: validates the style id, copies the two span words into a 0x84-byte stack record and fills the layout fields (same family as 0x18CEA4).
evidence: Disassembly shows a 0x84-byte frame, nine saved registers and the same 'style < 7 plus non-empty span' guard as Text_SpanHasContent, so the old 'ThrowArg' name (a tail call to a noreturn) was wrong.

name: Fs_IsArcOrTestShader
summary: Returns true when the archive entry name contains ".arc" or "nw_testshader"; used to skip/route container entries during a directory walk.
evidence: The two literals sit right behind the function (0x0018FC5C ".arc", 0x0018FC64 "nw_testshader") and the body is push + two strstr calls, so the name is exact; the parameter is a path string, not an fs handle.

name: Fs_IsBchPath
summary: Returns true when the given path contains the model suffix ".bch".
evidence: The literal ".bch" is stored immediately behind the function (0x001943B0) and is loaded into r1 before the std_strstr call, so the old 'Storage_IsPresent' name was wrong - this is a path-suffix test.

name: Fs_IsPtclPath
summary: Returns true when the given path contains the particle suffix ".ptcl".
evidence: The literal ".ptcl" is stored immediately behind the function (0x001E6C34) and passed to std_strstr, so this is a file-type test rather than a generic Str_Contains wrapper.

name: Ui_IsChipLayoutPath
summary: Returns true when the given layout path contains the chip-layout suffix ".chp".
evidence: The literal ".chp" is in the function's own literal pool at 0x002BD598 and the body is push + std_strstr + setne, confirming the previous guess.

name: Fs_IsSndqPath
summary: Returns true when the given path contains the sound-queue suffix ".sndq".
evidence: The literal ".sndq" sits behind the function at 0x00315ED4 and is passed to std_strstr; the old 'Ui_CheckGlobalString' name had neither the subsystem nor the tested string right.

name: Fs_IsEpiPath
summary: Returns true when the given path contains the effect suffix ".epi".
evidence: The literal ".epi" is stored behind the function at 0x0046CFA8 and fed to std_strstr, which rules out the old 'IsTextLayoutBusy' reading completely.

name: Fs_IsBinstPath
summary: Returns true when the given path contains the instance suffix ".binst".
evidence: The literal ".binst" is stored behind the function at 0x004B3618 and passed to std_strstr, so this is a file-type predicate, not a generic 'HasMatch' helper.

name: Fs_IsAniPath
summary: Returns true when the given path contains the animation suffix ".ani".
evidence: The literal ".ani" sits behind the function at 0x00576CD4 and is loaded into r1 before std_strstr, so the unknown 'tag' of the previous pass is now known.

name: Ui_MenuUpdate
summary: Per-frame menu update: invokes the screen's per-frame callback, decays the repeat timer, polls the input/action object, then runs the callback dispatch, text blink, detail refresh and pane update.
evidence: The callee list is now named (Ui_TextBlink_Update, maybe_Ui_DispatchCallback, maybe_Ui_EquipmentWindow_RefreshDetail) and matches the standard menu-screen frame step.

name: maybe_Ui_JumonWindow_DispatchVirtual
signature: void maybe_Ui_JumonWindow_DispatchVirtual(UiJumonWindow* self, int arg2, int handler)
summary: Per-frame update of the spell window that mirrors Ui_MenuUpdate and then dispatches the handler triple stored for the current mode at self+0x13C.
evidence: It has the same frame-step prologue as the named Ui_MenuUpdate, but the 0x13C handler array and the mode field are still unread, so 'DispatchVirtual' remains a description of the shape rather than of the action.

name: Ui_PanelNode_Init
summary: Initialises a panel node: clears the open byte, sets state 0x13, asks the owner (vtable+0x14) for slot 1 and clears the two list fields.
evidence: The caller is now named Ui_WindowResource_ResetAndInit, which initialises the panel nodes of a window resource, so the initialiser reading is supported.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_ShowSimple
summary: Sets the message window up for a simple message: stores the record word at +0x136 and selects state 7, style 2 and field 6; the decompilation then hits a bad instruction.
evidence: Callers now include maybe_Ui_StatusWindow_UpdateState and maybe_Ui_SceneFlow_SetState, which supports a show-message path, but Ghidra truncates the body at halt_baddata so the rest of the setup is unknown.

name: maybe_Gfx_Sprite2D_RefreshTouchInfo
summary: Refreshes the object's touch record: builds the 12-byte (type, kind, id, x, y) record with kind 2 from the position and mesh id and caches it at +0x4D8..+0x4E0.
evidence: Five sibling classes in this batch have byte-identical bodies differing only in the kind passed to 0x0040DBB4 (2/3/4/6/7/10), and 0x00423794 turns that record into a heap touch event - so these cache touch info rather than 'read geometry'.

name: maybe_Gfx_Sprite2D_RefreshTouchInfoB
summary: Second variant of the touch-record refresh (kind 10) for the state-4 sprite: resets the draw state with 0x4DD70C and caches the record at +0x3B8..+0x3C0.
evidence: Same body as 0x001A3E68 apart from the kind and the destination offset, and the shared 0x0040DBB4 helper builds a touch event record, so the old 'ReadGeometryB' wording was wrong.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_RefreshTouchInfo
summary: Refreshes a widget's touch record (kind 4) and copies it plus the resolved frame-table row fields into +0x4D8..+0x4F4.
evidence: The body uses the same 0x0040DBB4 touch-record builder as its siblings but also resolves a frame-table row with 0x5923A0, so it stores touch info for a widget rather than loading a sprite frame.

name: maybe_Actor2D_RefreshTouchInfo
summary: Refreshes the 2D actor's touch record with kind 7 from its position and mesh id, caching the six fields at +0x4D8..+0x4E0.
evidence: Identical to the other five touch-record refreshers in this batch (only the kind differs) and 0x0040DBB4 builds a tagged touch event, which rules out the old 'QueryGroundInfo' reading.

name: maybe_Ui_Sprite_RefreshTouchInfo
summary: Refreshes the sprite's touch record with kind 3 and caches it at +0x4D8..+0x4E0.
evidence: Same template as 0x001A3E68/0x0021B6F0 with the kind 3 argument; the shared builder produces a touch event, so 'GetSpriteColorAndOffsets' was a misread.

name: maybe_Field_Gadget_RefreshTouchInfo
summary: Refreshes the field gadget's touch record with kind 6 and caches it at +0x4D8..+0x4E0.
evidence: Same six-field body as the other touch-record refreshers, only the kind differs; nothing in it converts to gadget-local coordinates as the old name claimed.

name: Field_Object2D_CreateTouchEvent
signature: int Field_Object2D_CreateTouchEvent(u8* out, u32 arg2, u32 b, u32* point, u32 id)
summary: Allocates a 0x14-byte touch event record, stores type 1 and the id, fills the 12-byte event body via 0x0040DBB4 and returns the record.
evidence: Its caller is now named maybe_Field_SceneObject_QueryState and the body allocates + fills exactly the record shape the sibling refreshers cache, so the 'touch event' reading is consistent.

name: maybe_Gfx_Sprite2D_Refresh
summary: Thin refresh wrapper that calls 0x0062AE90 (rebuilds the draw node from the sprite state) and returns 0; the Thumb decompilation is incomplete.
evidence: No callers and the recovered body is only the call plus 'return 0', so the name describes the intended role rather than the recovered behaviour.

name: Ui_TextStyle_GetDescriptor
summary: Lazily allocates the array of five style descriptors and returns the descriptor body for styleId (style+0x60 plus the length word); null for ids >= 5.
evidence: Three callers are now named, including maybe_Ui_Window_RefreshMessageArgsA/B and Ui_RecipeInfo_ShowCraftMessage, which all need the text style descriptor.

name: Ui_Object_SetNamedDrawParam
signature: void Ui_Object_SetNamedDrawParam(UiObject* self, const char* name, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5, u32 arg6)
summary: Sets a named draw parameter on the object's render node: resolves the name through the owner's vtable +0x2C and forwards the value plus four arguments to 0x001D7F50.
evidence: The caller is now named Ui_TimeWindow_BindPanes and passes a named pane/material parameter, which supports the 'named draw parameter' reading.

name: Ui_Node_FindBaseChild
summary: Looks up the child named "base" through the node's vtable +0x2C, dispatches into it when found, and otherwise stores the default value from 0x007A9318.
evidence: The literal 0x0065736162 ("base") is passed to the name query in the body, so the 'FindBaseChild' name is exact.

name: Ui_Object_ReleaseChildList
summary: Releases every element of the intrusive child list at +0x20 by calling its virtual destructor (vtable slot +4).
evidence: This is a byte-for-byte copy of 0x1BBECC only with the sentinel at +0x20, and its caller is now named BattleScene_ReleaseUnitSlotHandles; encoding the offset in the name ('List20') was unreadable.

name: maybe_Ui_ItemScreen_ToggleCursor
summary: Handles the item screen's input bits: on bit 1 it forwards the cursor triple, on bits 0x102 it recomputes the cursor offset from the row and page size and selects the entry, on bit 4 it resets the cursor to 0xFF.
evidence: The body clearly drives the list cursor from input flags, but 'ToggleCursor' only covers one of the three branches and the class is still assumed, so the name stays provisional.

name: maybe_Ui_ItemScreen_CloseList
summary: Closes the item list sub-view: resets the list, reads the selected member id and chains to Ui_TextScroll_End, then stores the two handler words.
evidence: The callees are now named (Ui_ListCursor_GetSelectedMemberId, Ui_TextScroll_End), which supports the close/select reading, but no caller or vtable slot confirms that this is the item screen.

name: Ui_ShopItemList_OpenList
summary: Opens the shop list: resets the row list, seeds the selection (id 0xFFFF, offset -1, count 1) and stores the first handler pair.
evidence: The standard list-open sequence is visible through the now-named Ui_ListCursor_GetSelectedMemberId / Ui_TextScroll_End and the immediate 0xFFFF/-1 defaults.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_SetMode
signature: void maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_SetMode(UiMessageWindow* self, u32 layoutIndex, u32 arg3)
summary: Selects the message-window mode (single/double layout), rebuilds the panes for that mode and hides both sides.
evidence: The decompilation loses the self argument and several registers (unaff_r4/r5/r7/r8), so despite the now-named Ui_MessageWindow_RebuildPanes callee the mode field's meaning is unverified.

name: Ui_MessageText_ResetChildren
summary: Resets the two page objects at self+8 and self+0xC by calling their virtual slot +0x18 with 0.
evidence: It is adjacent to the now-named Ui_MessageText_Update and uses the same (*(vt+0x18))(obj,0) detach idiom as the message-window constructor's child teardown.

name: Object_MarkReleased
summary: Releases the child object at +0x10 when the owner lookup still resolves, then marks the child dead by setting its byte +0x25D.
evidence: The caller is now named Gfx_ScreenView_ReleaseAll, which releases the screen view's objects, and the body writes the dead flag after the release call.

name: Actor_ReleaseLinkedModelAttachments
summary: Releases the model attach slots (+0x40 and +0x48) of the object linked through the actor's +0x110 handle, after validating the handle generation.
evidence: The callee is now confidently named Model_AttachSlot_Release, so the routine releases attachments rather than 'getting' the linked object as the old name said.

name: maybe_Ui_Billboard_UpdateFromActor
summary: Places a billboard sprite from its owning actor: releases a stale attach slot, copies the actor position/scale into the sprite transform and applies the global fade/rotation constants.
evidence: Its vtable slot and the 0x7E709C transform constants are visible, but the owning class is still unknown and the named callee only covers the release half.

name: Battle_ActionAnim_UseItemElement_Play
summary: Performs the item-use animation: releases both equipment attach slots of the actor's model and asks the actor to play the action named "UseItem" through vtable +0x84.
evidence: The literal "UseItem" is stored at 0x004005F8 inside the function and the callee is the now-named Model_AttachSlot_Release, so the old guess is exact.

name: Actor_HandleAnimEvent
summary: Animation-event hook: for event 0xA7 it flips the mirror flag via vtable +0x90/+0x3C, and for events 0x50..0x58 it calls the variant-apply slot +0x178; everything else is ignored after the common 0x2785C8 pre-call.
evidence: The pre-call callee is now named Actor_AnimEvent_EnableSlotFlag (0.7) and its evidence names this function as its caller, which fixes the animation-event context.

name: Actor_ResetSlotTable
summary: Clears the four 0x20-byte slot records to their empty sentinels (1, -1, 0xFF, 0xFFFF) and then calls the actor's vtable +0xBC reset hook.
evidence: The caller is now named Battle_ResetUnitStates, which resets the unit state tables before a battle, so the slot-table reset reading is supported.

name: maybe_Actor_PlayHookSe
summary: Validates the actor's +0x110 handle, calls Field_Actor_SetMotionState on the linked object and then posts sound effect 0x2F on it.
evidence: The two callees are now named (Field_Actor_SetMotionState, and 0x5E7848 which also posts 0x2F), so 'play a step/hook sound' is plausible but the 'hook' part is still unverified.

name: Ui_Slot_ResetDefaults
summary: Resets a pooled UI slot: releases the child at +0x60 through vtable +0x38, sets alpha 0xFF and frame 4, and copies the two default 3-float vectors.
evidence: Both callers are now named (maybe_Ui_ItemSelect_ReleaseAllSlots and Ui_ItemSelect_RemoveSlotById), which recycle slot entries and need exactly this reset.

name: maybe_Model_UpdateFaceAnimation
signature: void maybe_Model_UpdateFaceAnimation(void* self, int face, int frame)
summary: Copies the requested face and frame table rows into the character's 0x158-byte face records, skipping the 0xFF 'no change' values.
evidence: The callers are now named Model_SetFaceMode and maybe_Model_UpdateBlinkTimer, which supports the face reading; the decompilation still loses a register (unaff_r4), so the record indexing stays partly inferred.

name: maybe_Field_ObjectCtor
summary: Constructor of a field object with sub-objects: base-initialises through 0x004712D0, installs the class vtable, seeds the default vectors and chains the three sub-constructors 0x2F2678, 0x3DAE90 and 0x4AC9B0.
evidence: The body is a constructor chain, but the old name embedded the raw vtable address (vt1D6C98) which is unreadable and meaningless to a modder; no caller (factory table) so the class stays unidentified.

name: Ui_Widget_IsTouchActive
summary: Advances the widget's touch record at +0x4D8 through Field_Object2D_RunTouchTransition and reports whether it has not reached the finished state 3.
evidence: The +0x4D8 record is the touch record filled by the RefreshTouchInfo family in this batch and advanced by the named Field_Object2D_RunTouchTransition, so 'sprite busy' was the wrong object.

name: maybe_Game_IsStateFlagClear
summary: Calls the state predicate 0x0064DB08 with the argument and returns its logical negation.
evidence: Nothing in the body mentions battle and 0x64DB08 is still unnamed, so the old 'IsNotBattleState' name claimed a specific state that cannot be verified; the leading 0x423648 call is likely a mis-attributed tail call.

name: Gfx_BuildBillboardQuad
signature: u32 Gfx_BuildBillboardQuad(UIWidget* self, float* out, u32* uv, u32 animId, u32 frame)
summary: Builds the four transformed corners of a billboard quad plus its normalised edge directions and the frame width/height, writing them into the caller's 17-word output block.
evidence: Its callers are now named Actor_UpdateTrailQuad and Field_Marker_DrawOverlay, so this is the shared 3D billboard quad builder, not a UI sprite routine.

name: maybe_Ui_Anim_GetFrame
summary: Returns the current frame index of the object's +0xAB0 animation/movie handle (0x500084/0x4FFB34), clamped to >= 0, or the cached +0xACC value when no explicit frame is stored.
evidence: The callers are now named Movie_GetFrame and maybe_Ui_DebugMenu_CheckFrameSpike, which confirms the frame meaning but not whether the owner is the movie player or a UI animator.

name: maybe_Gfx_MoviePlayer_Dtor
summary: Destructor that installs the two class vtables, releases the owned block at +0x454, destroys the sub-objects at words 4 and 5 and frees the object.
evidence: No caller; the sub-object at word 4 is torn down through the currently named Text_NgWord_CloseService, which makes a pure 'movie player' identity doubtful, so the name stays provisional.

name: maybe_Gfx_CreateNodeA
summary: Constructor wrapper that allocates through 0x001B79EC and installs the class vtable 0x75A4EC; it is registered as one of the NPC action classes.
evidence: Its caller is now named Field_RegisterNpcActions, which registers the class in the NPC action table, so it is a class constructor rather than a general 'create node'; the class itself is unidentified.

name: maybe_Gfx_CreateRenderNodeC
summary: Constructor wrapper: allocates through 0x001B79EC, installs vtable 0x75C378 and seeds the default fields at +0x2C..+0x50; registered by Field_RegisterNpcActions.
evidence: Callers are now named (Field_RegisterNpcActions and maybe_Field_CreateSmallEffect), which places it among the field action-class constructors; the class identity is still unknown.

name: maybe_Field_CreateNpcActionC
summary: Tiny constructor: allocates through 0x001B79EC and installs the class vtable 0x75FA64; it is registered as one of the NPC action classes.
evidence: Its caller is now named Field_RegisterNpcActions, so the old 'Ui_CreateObjectVariantA' prefix pointed at the wrong subsystem; the class behaviour is still unknown.

name: maybe_Gfx_CreateNodeB
summary: Constructor wrapper that allocates through 0x001B7D60, installs vtable 0x75A520 and sets the default value 0.26 at +0x30; registered by Field_RegisterActorActions.
evidence: Its caller is now named Field_RegisterActorActions, so it is an actor action-class constructor; the class itself is unidentified.

name: maybe_Gfx_CreateRenderNodeD
summary: Constructor wrapper: allocates through 0x001B7D60, installs vtable 0x75C3AC and seeds the default fields (0x7E7000 vector, 1.8f); registered by Field_RegisterActorActions.
evidence: Caller is now named Field_RegisterActorActions, placing it among the actor action-class constructors; the class identity is unknown.

name: Field_ActorTurnActionCtor
summary: Constructor of the field-actor turn action: allocates through 0x294BD4, installs vtable 0x765638 and sets the turn speed/angle defaults.
evidence: Its caller is now named Field_RegisterActorActions and the vtable neighbour slot is the turn-animation update, so the turn-action reading is supported.

name: Field_ActorAimPoseActionCtor
summary: Constructor of the field-actor aim-pose action: allocates through 0x294BD4, installs vtable 0x76AC70 and sets the pose defaults.
evidence: Its caller is now named Field_RegisterActorActions and the vtable's slot 2 is the aim-pose IK update, which supports the old guess.

name: Field_ActorMove_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the field actor-move action: runs Actor_Action_InitDescriptor, installs vtable 0x75A5C4, clears the state and seeds the default timer pair.
evidence: Its caller is now named Actor_CreateActionTable, so this is one of the action-class constructors; 'InitDefaults' hid that it is the class constructor, and struct initialisation alone was the previous reading.

name: maybe_FlwAction_Ctor
summary: Constructor that runs Actor_Action_InitDescriptor and installs the flw action vtable (g_flwActionVtable).
evidence: The installed vtable is already symbolised as g_flwActionVtable, so the class is identifiable; 'InstallVtable' described the mechanism instead of the class and its caller Actor_CreateActionTable confirms it is a constructor.

name: maybe_Actor_Action_CreateJump2
summary: Creates action-table entry type 4: vtable g_actorActionCurveMove2Vtable, opcode field 4, the extra callback at +0x4C and the embedded transform from 0x17C4CC.
evidence: Its caller is now named Actor_CreateActionTable, confirming it is an action-class constructor; whether the class is a 'jump' or a curve move is still open (the vtable symbol says curve move).

name: maybe_Field_ActionState_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a field action-state entry: runs Actor_Action_InitDescriptor, installs vtable 0x762850, copies the two default vectors and sets the state ids 1 and 2.
evidence: Its caller is now named Actor_CreateActionTable, so a plain state entry is certain, but nothing in the body mentions carrying as the old 'InitCarry' name claimed.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_CtorSimple
summary: Constructor of a small field actor/action object: allocates through Actor_Action_InitDescriptor, installs vtable 0x7658F8 and initialises the state bytes to 0xFF/0xFF/0.
evidence: Its caller is now named Actor_CreateActionTable, which shows it is an action-class constructor rather than a field actor; the class itself is unidentified.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_CtorSimpleB
summary: Second small constructor of the same family: allocates through Actor_Action_InitDescriptor, installs vtable 0x76592C and copies the two default words.
evidence: Its caller is now named Actor_CreateActionTable; like its sibling it is an action-class constructor whose behaviour is not identifiable from the body.

name: ActorAction_CreateMoveAction
summary: Constructor of the scripted move action: installs g_fieldActorActionMoveVtable, sets opcode 4, seeds the 0xFF/0xFFFF sentinels and builds the embedded transform; returns base-0x58.
evidence: Its caller is now named Actor_CreateActionTable and the installed vtable is already symbolised as g_fieldActorActionMoveVtable, so the move-action reading is supported.

name: Field_ActorAction_CreateTurnState
summary: Constructor of the turn-toward action state: installs vtable 0x76DEC8, sets opcode 2, seeds the 0xFF/0xFFFF sentinels and builds the embedded transform; returns base-0x58.
evidence: Its caller is now named Actor_CreateActionTable and the body's opcode plus the transform builder match the other action-state constructors.

name: Actor_Action_Trail_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the trail action: runs Actor_Action_InitDescriptor, installs g_actorActionTrailVtable and zeroes the trail offsets.
evidence: The caller is now named Actor_CreateActionTable and the installed vtable is already symbolised as g_actorActionTrailVtable.

name: Actor_Action_TrailB_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the second trail action: runs Actor_Action_InitDescriptor, installs g_actorActionTrailVtableB and zeroes the trail arrays.
evidence: The caller is now named Actor_CreateActionTable and the installed vtable is already symbolised as g_actorActionTrailVtableB.

name: maybe_ActorAction_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor: calls the action base destructor 0x294C88 and frees the object with 0x10F6CC.
evidence: Its vtable slot 0 sits in the actor-action vtable group and the cluster is made of named Actor_Action_* deleting destructors; no UI table is involved, so the old 'Ui_Table_' prefix was wrong.

name: maybe_Field_ActorMove_DtorThunkC
summary: Deleting destructor of an actor-move class: stores the vtable argument, runs the base destructor 0x294C88 and frees the object with 0x10F6CC.
evidence: No caller; the body is the standard deleting-destructor pair, but which of the two 0x1E16xx/0x1E1Bxx classes it belongs to cannot be told from the body.

name: maybe_Field_ActorMove_DtorThunkD
summary: Deleting destructor of the sibling actor-move class: stores the vtable argument, runs the base destructor 0x294C88 and frees the object.
evidence: Same callee sequence as 0x1E160C in a 4-byte larger frame and no caller, so it cannot be attributed to a specific class.

name: Actor_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of the Actor class: runs the base teardown 0x294C88 and frees the object.
evidence: The referenced vtable 0x75C59C is the Actor vtable (it also lists maybe_Actor_Dtor and Actor_CreateActionTable), so the class is known; renamed to the project's DtorDelete convention.

name: Actor_Action_DtorDeleteC
summary: Deleting destructor of an actor action: stores the vtable argument, runs the shared action destructor 0x294C88 and frees the object.
evidence: It sits immediately after the actor-action vtable slot at 0x2C09F0 and uses the same destructor pair as the other named action destructors.

name: Monster_BehaviorAction_DtorDelete
summary: Scalar deleting destructor: stores the vtable argument, runs the action base destructor and frees the block.
evidence: It sits between the now-named Monster_BehaviorAction_Ctor and the actor lookup helpers, and the body is the standard deleting-destructor pair.

name: Field_ActorAction_DtorDeleteM
summary: Scalar deleting destructor with a vtable argument: stores the vptr, runs the action base destructor 0x294C88 and frees the block.
evidence: Its neighbours are Field_ActorAction_Ctor and maybe_Field_DragonJumpAction_Update, which fixes the class family.

name: Field_DragonJumpAction_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of the dragon-jump action: calls the base destructor 0x1E1624 and frees the object.
evidence: It sits directly after Field_DragonJumpActionCtor (0x3E5008) and before the jump update, and calls that class's destructor.

name: Ui_Object_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of a UI object subclass: stores the vptr, runs the list-aware base destructor and frees the object.
evidence: It is slot 0 of the vtable in the 0x776BEC region and the only vptr-taking destructor in that block, next to the named poker-window code.

name: maybe_Ui_PanelRow_RegisterInList
summary: Passes a one-element argument block containing itself to the list routine at self+0x38.
evidence: The callee 0x295558 is now named Ui_CompositeWindow_DrawPanes, which conflicts with the previous 'list insert/notify' reading, so the name is left as a maybe with that contradiction recorded.

name: maybe_Ui_PanelState_AdvanceFromModelB
summary: Variant of the panel advance: when the effect and flags allow it, applies the model loop, sets state 0x11, rebinds the slot and copies the two timers.
evidence: Its sibling 0x1E31C8 and the named callees (Ui_PokerDisplayWindow_PlayLoop1, maybe_Ui_Slot_BindControl) support the advance reading, but the 'from model' wording is still the previous pass's inference.

name: Container_StringMap_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the string-map container: allocates the header, installs g_stringMapBase, builds the sub-container, links the self-referencing list and fills the twelve 0xFF index slots.
evidence: The installed globals are already symbolised as g_stringMapBase and g_stringMapDescriptor, and its neighbours are Container_StringHashMapInsert/BuildStringMap.

name: Sound_SetStreamVolumeByHandle
signature: u8 Sound_SetStreamVolumeByHandle(SoundSystem* self, u32 handle, u32 volume, int reset)
summary: Applies a volume to the stream behind a sound voice handle, optionally resetting the stream position first; returns 1 when the handle is valid.
evidence: The handle validation (0x711090, tag 0xE), the stream field at +0xC and the 0x542804/0x5427B0 stream calls all match the already named sound-stream setters.

name: Sound_ReleaseFileSlot
signature: void Sound_ReleaseFileSlot(SoundSystem* self, u32 index, u32 arg3, u32 overrides)
summary: Releases an entry of the sound file cache: stops its sequence player, clears the 0x13C-byte slot, clears the occupancy bit and decrements the use counter.
evidence: The callee is now named Sound_SequencePlayer_Reset and the body clears exactly the slot the 0x1EE294 allocator hands out, so the release reading is supported.

name: maybe_Sound_SetVoicePan
signature: u32 maybe_Sound_SetVoicePan(SoundSystem* self, u32 handle, float pan)
summary: Validates the voice handle and writes the pan value to the engine voice's +0xCC field.
evidence: The write target +0xCC and the handle validation match the other sound setters, but the incoming pan register is lost (in_s0) and no caller confirms the parameter, so it stays a maybe.

name: Work_GetRecordU16At
signature: u16 Work_GetRecordU16At(u32 id, int index, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Returns one of the four 16-bit fields of the data-manager record for the given id: index 0/1/2/3 selects byte offsets 0x0/0x4/0x8/0xC.
evidence: The body resolves the record through Game_GetDataManager + 0x63F108 and the four-way index arithmetic is complete in the decompilation; only the record type is unknown.

name: Work_GetRecordByteAt
signature: u8 Work_GetRecordByteAt(u32 id, int index, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Returns the byte at +2 of the 4-byte group selected by index (0..3) in the same data-manager record.
evidence: Complete body: Game_GetDataManager + 0x63F108 then +0/+4/+8/+0xC and a byte load at +2, which matches the four-field record layout used by 0x1F2F4C.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_GetAnchorForMember
signature: void maybe_Battle_Ui_GetAnchorForMember(BattleBalloonUi* self, int mode, int flag, u32 argument)
summary: Interpolates the member's anchor position (slot 0 transform or one of the two cached offsets) into the balloon object's screen fields.
evidence: The decompilation is damaged (in_s0/in_d8/in_d9), and although the mixer is clear the class and the anchor index are not, so the name keeps its maybe_ prefix.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_GetPartyCenter
signature: void maybe_Battle_Ui_GetPartyCenter(float* out, PartyMember* member, int argument, u32 argument2)
summary: Counts the non-null members of the 16-slot array, asks each for its anchor world position and writes the centre of the resulting bounds.
evidence: The body's min/max arithmetic is mangled (one term is computed as fVar7-fVar7), so although the bounding-box centre idea is visible the result cannot be verified.

name: maybe_FieldParty_SelectFormationSlot
signature: void maybe_FieldParty_SelectFormationSlot(PartyGroup* group, int mode, int target, int slot)
summary: Selects a formation slot for a member and, when more than one member is present, reruns the balloon layout for the whole group.
evidence: The callee is now named Battle_Ui_LayoutBalloons, which confirms the layout half, but the 'formation slot' choice is only the vtable +0x40 call and remains inferred.

name: FieldParty_CalcMemberWorldPosition
signature: void FieldParty_CalcMemberWorldPosition(PartyGroup* group, int mode, int slot)
summary: Computes a member's world position: takes the member transform, applies the group origin offsets (0x574044) and adds the mode-specific offset vector (0x574224).
evidence: Complete body with named transform callees and three explicit modes (member 0 / +0x37 / +0x40), which matches 'calculate member world position'.

name: maybe_Ui_SetLinkedHandleFlag
signature: void maybe_Ui_SetLinkedHandleFlag(UiPart* self, u32 handle, u8 flag)
summary: If the passed handle is still live in the global handle table, notifies the currently bound object (vtable +0x7C) and then stores the boolean at +0x234.
evidence: The body never stores the handle itself - it only validates it and writes a flag - so 'BindObjectHandle' promised a binding that is not there; the same idiom appears in 0x2117C4/0x2128D0.

name: maybe_Ui_CreateTextWidget
summary: Constructor wrapper: calls the shared UI object constructor and installs vtable 0x75B978.
evidence: The vtable neighbours (0x213084/0x21309C/0x2130F8) are text-layer routines, which supports 'text widget', but no caller or string confirms the class.

name: maybe_Ui_CreatePaneWidget
summary: Constructor wrapper: calls the shared UI object constructor and installs vtable 0x75D210.
evidence: The vtable slots share the base-class pane routines with the text widget, which supports 'pane widget', but no caller confirms the class.

name: maybe_Ui_CreateObjectVariantC
summary: Tiny derived-class constructor: calls the shared UI object constructor and installs vtable 0x761344.
